title: Queue Horizon: weekly catchup
content:
Meeting: Serving runtime weekly catchup - Queue Horizon
Date: 2027-04-06
Attendees: Ava Chen (owner), Marcus Patel, Riley Gomez, Priya Nair, Ethan Brooks, oncall: S. Vega
Duration: 45m

Summary:
- Quick sync on kernel concurrency changes, KV cache warmup pilot, and batching policy experiments.
- Emphasis this week on reducing p95 tail during small-concurrency bursts and improving cache hit for cold-start short requests.
- Three follow-ups: a narrow kernel rollback guard, a KV warmup tuning pass, and an async microbatcher tweak.

Key metrics snapshot (rolling 24h):
- Global p50 token latency: 18ms (steady)
- Global p95 token latency: 210ms (up from 170ms last week)
- Throughput (tokens/s): 1.2M (hosted cluster pool)
- KV cache hit rate (session prefix): 62% overall, 43% for <8-token prompts
- Average batch size: 4.2 tokens/request; goal -> 5.5
- CPU steal events on kernel nodes: 0.7% -> flagged on node-group-a

What changed since last week:
1) Kernel concurrency gating (feature flag: concurrency-hedge-v2) rolled to 30% of traffic on cluster-beta. Observed: reduced queue length variance for long requests, but small short-lived requests saw an unexpected p95 increase during reorders. Hypothesis: gating introduced an extra enqueue-dequeue hop for microbatches which increased tail when batches missed coalescing windows.
2) KV cache warmup pilot on a subset of customers: we prefetch top-3 user-prefixes based on recency. Hit rate improved for long chat sessions (~+12% for sessions > 20 turns) but regressed for very short sessions (<8 tokens) due to aggressive eviction during memory pressure bursts.
3) Batching policy 'delay-3ms' A/B test ran for 36h. Average batch size increased by 8% in test, but end-to-end p95 for short prompts increased by 16ms. Need refined heuristics that are workload-aware.

Technical notes / experiments:
- Kernel patch (PR 789): introduced a per-core micro-queue for faster dequeue for latency-sensitive queues. Implementation uses a small lock-free ring buffer but we saw contention on CPU topology mismatches (node-group-a uses older kernels). Action: add CPU affinity pins for ring buffer poll threads (ENG-2151).
- Eviction shaping: current KV eviction is LRU-ish but favors size over recency. Experimented with a time-decay hybrid (recency*weight + size penalty). Result: modest improvement in hit rate stability but increases GC pressure. We should tune decay constant and run for 72h before broader rollout.
- Async microbatcher: moved to cooperative yielding when waiting for coalescing window to avoid busy-wait. Reduces CPU steal but increased latency for very small immediate requests when preemption happens. Plan: adaptive yield that short-circuits when pending-queue depth < 2. Ticket: ENG-2160.

Incidents and triage:
- 2027-04-04 03:12 UTC - short-lived p95 spike (~400ms) on cluster-beta. Root cause: sudden drop in batch coalescing due to a stray GC on node-group-a that evicted hot KV segments and temporarily reduced batch sizes. Remediation: revert concurrency-hedge-v2 rollout to 10% on node-group-a and reapply after affinity pins. Postmortem stub: INGEST-426 (owner: Riley).

Decisions made:
- Hold global rollout of concurrency-hedge-v2 until affinity pins and a 72h soak on newer kernels. Rollout target postponed to 2027-04-20.
- Continue KV warmup pilot but reduce prefetch aggressiveness (top-1 instead of top-3) and increase memory headroom by 10% on pilot nodes. Priya to own the tuning loop.
- Disable delay-3ms experiment for short prompt route; replace with an adaptive-delay experiment gated by request-size histogram.

Action items (owners + tickets):
- AVA: Draft rollout playbook for concurrency-hedge-v2 including rollback and metrics (ENG-2152). Due: 2027-04-09.
- MARCUS: Implement CPU affinity pins and test on staging; coordinate with infra for kernel upgrade plan (ENG-2151). Due: 2027-04-08.
- PRIYA: Adjust KV warmup to top-1 prefetch, iterate decay constant, run 72h soak, update dashboard. (ENG-2165). Due: 2027-04-13.
- RILEY: Postmortem for 2027-04-04 incident (INGEST-426), include timeline and suggested alarms for eviction rate. Due: 2027-04-11.
- ETHAN: Prototype adaptive microbatch yield heuristic and open a PR for perf benching (ENG-2160). Due: 2027-04-12.

Follow-ups / discussion topics for next week:
- Evaluate a hybrid batching window that varies per-route based on recent effective batch size. Need simulation and offline replay to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Consider a small persistent warm cache for very short prompts (cold-start heavy customers) — tradeoff memory vs token cost; propose a pilot for customers in low-latency tier.
- Alerting: add an SLO guard for "batch size < 3" sustained for 5m for any route -> automatic rollback of delay heuristics.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep watch on node-group-a kernel upgrades timeline; infra is currently booked for kernel rollouts 2027-04-18 -> may push our full rollout.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime ops has a side-discussion about whether prefetch should be per-customer or global hot-list. Strong leaning toward per-customer but need cost modeling.

Attachments / references:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (kernel microqueue)
- Experiment graphs: internal dashboard link (confluence:ServingRuntime/QueueHorizonNotes)
- Incident log: INGEST-426

Next sync: 2027-04-13 10:00 PT (same standup slot).

-- end of notes --
